subject: g++ 4.2, ADL, mdivide_left_tri, & partial template instantiation

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: g++ 4.2, ADL, mdivide_left_tri, & partial template instantiation
parts:
Yatta! I isolated a simple test case, then
figured out why multiply was different than
mdivide_left_tri, and even have a sketch of a
solution that works -- but it'll take a bit of
work to refactor what's there and I'm out for
the next few days.

To make a long story short, the problem really
does seem to be a bug in g++ 4.2's argument-dependent lookup:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argument-dependent_name_lookup

Specifically, an interaction with partially specifying
types during type inference and argument-dependent lookup.

I started by isolating a minimal test case with the same error
as we saw for the inv_wishart model compilation:

--------------------
#include <stan/math/matrix.hpp>
#include <stan/agrad/matrix.hpp>

int main() {
using stan::agrad::var;

Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var, Eigen::Dynamic, Eigen::Dynamic> I;
Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var, Eigen::Dynamic, Eigen::Dynamic> L;

// fails to compile w/o agrad; with math, gives our warning message
using stan::agrad::mdivide_left_tri;
using stan::math::mdivide_left_tri;
L = mdivide_left_tri<Eigen::Lower>(L,I);

// works fine
L = multiply(I,L);
}
-----------------------

I put the above in a file ~/stan/test.cc,
made libstan.a, then did this:

~/stan> g++ -O0 -Lbin -lstan -Isrc -Ilib test.cpp

Everything compiles fine. multiply() works even
without the using statement. That's what's supposed to happen
with argument-dependent lookup.

If you get rid of the using statement for agrad::mdivide_left_tri,
you get the same error message we've been getting for inv_wishart
in the tests with the long template lists. But, if you get rid
of the math::mdivide_left_tri using, you only get a function
not found error.

The question remains as to why mdivide_left_tri() doesn't work
when multiply() does. But if you look at the test cases in
the code above, it's obvious -- there's an explicit partial
template instantiation in the call to mdivide_left_tri and
none in multiply.

So I took the original definition:

template<int TriView,int R1,int C1,int R2,int C2>
inline Eigen::Matrix<var,R1,C2> mdivide_left_tri(const Eigen::Matrix<var,R1,C1> &A,
const Eigen::Matrix<var,R2,C2> &b) {
if (A.cols() != A.rows())
throw std::invalid_argument("A is not square");
if (A.cols() != b.rows())
throw std::invalid_argument("A.cols() != b.rows()");
return A.template triangularView<TriView>().solve(b);
}

and added a variant with a hard-coded Eigen::Lower on the last line:

template <int R1,int C1,int R2,int C2>
inline Eigen::Matrix<var,R1,C2> mdivide_left_tri2(const Eigen::Matrix<var,R1,C1> &A,
const Eigen::Matrix<var,R2,C2> &b) {
if (A.cols() != A.rows())
throw std::invalid_argument("A is not square");
if (A.cols() != b.rows())
throw std::invalid_argument("A.cols() != b.rows()");
return A.template triangularView<Eigen::Lower>().solve(b);
}

I added

L = mdivide_left_tri2(L,I);

to the test program, and Bob's your uncle.*

Unfortunately, this hard-codes the view into the function.
But if we want to run on g++ 4.2 (and it is the default
with the usual Mac developer tools and so will probably
be the defualt in R), I don't see an alternative
at this point.

Can we just hardcode triangularView for lower-triangular views
for now? If not, we can add both. And there are all the
other similar functions.

- Bob

* http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob's_your_uncle
